title: The Event Monitoring & Notification API: what it does, access, headers and limits

what-it-is.statement: The Event Monitoring & Notification API is a shared service for monitoring, alerting and automated response across Zscaler products, including ZIA, ZPA and Data Protection, delivering notifications by email, webhook or Amazon SNS.

quotes: Event Monitoring & Notification API is a shared service that delivers real-time monitoring, alerting, and automated response capabilities across Zscaler products, including Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA), Zscaler Private Access (ZPA), and Data Protection.
supports multiple notification channels, including email, webhook, and Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS).

capabilities.statement: It offers a service catalog of sources, source types and source events navigated through HATEOAS links, and subscriptions to specific events; the catalog is hierarchical, Sources, then Source Types, then Source Events.

quotes: Service catalog: Browse available sources, source types, and source events using Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State (HATEOAS) links.
Subscription management: Subscribe to specific events to receive alerts and notifications when matching events occur.
The service catalog is hierarchical: Sources → Source Types → Source Events.

operations.statement: The repository's structural validation of the captured contract counts 15 operations on 12 paths for Event Monitoring, including catalog reads under `/catalog/sources`; the API is not in the generated surface layer, so the operation list is read from the OpenAPI capture.

This report is structural validation for the inline OpenAPI snapshot.

prerequisites.statement: The service must be enabled for the tenant by the Zscaler account team, and the API client needs the Event Monitoring Subscribe role (view-only on the catalog, full access to subscriptions) plus a role from the product resource whose notifications it subscribes to.

quotes: Ensure that you have the Event Monitoring & Notification API service enabled for your tenant. To obtain access to this API service, contact your Zscaler Account team.

Register the API client application in Authentication Service and assign the Event Monitoring Subscribe role. This role provides view-only access to the service catalog and full access to subscriptions (i.e., create, update, and delete) within the Event Monitoring & Notification API.
Assign a role from the API product resource for which the notifications are subscribed.

zpa-only-today.statement: The guide says notifications can currently be subscribed for ZPA, so a ZPA product-resource role is required.

quotes: Currently, you can subscribe to notifications for ZPA, so a role from the ZPA product resource must be assigned.

tenant-headers.statement: Every subscription call needs `x-em-cloud` (the product tenant's cloud, for example prod.zpath.net) and `x-em-tenant` (the product tenant ID); monitoring several product tenants takes separate subscriptions with different headers.

quotes: In addition, all subscription API calls require the following headers to identify the product tenant that you want to monitor:
- x-em-cloud: Cloud identifier for the product tenant (e.g., prod.zpath.net)
- x-em-tenant: Product tenant identifier for ZIA, ZPA, etc. (e.g., 145254691217866752)
You can monitor multiple Zscaler services by creating separate subscriptions with different headers (x-em-cloud and x-em-tenant) for each product tenant.

rate-limit.statement: All Event Monitoring endpoints are limited to 1,000 calls per second per tenant; responses carry `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining` and `x-ratelimit-reset`, documented here as Unix epoch seconds.

quotes: All endpoints within the Event Monitoring & Notification API are subject to a rate limit of 1,000 calls per second, per tenant.
- x-ratelimit-limit: The rate limit ceiling that is applicable for the current API request.
- x-ratelimit-remaining: The number of API requests remaining for the current rate limit window.
- x-ratelimit-reset: The time (in Unix epoch seconds) remaining in the current window, after which the rate limit resets.

error-codes.statement: It returns 400 `BAD_REQUEST` for malformed JSON or missing subscription fields (name, description, scope, channels, enabled), 401 `UNAUTHORIZED`, 403 `FORBIDDEN` for an insufficient role, 404 `NOT_FOUND` for an unknown source key or subscription ID, 429 `RATE_LIMITED` and 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`, for which Support wants the response's correlation_id.

quotes: | 400 | BAD_REQUEST | Malformed JSON or required fields are missing in the subscription request |
name, description, scope, channels, and enabled.
| 401 | UNAUTHORIZED | Missing or invalid bearer token |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | Valid token with insufficient scope or role |
| 404 | NOT_FOUND | Resource does not exist. This error could occur due to incorrect source key, subscription ID, etc. |
| 429 | RATE_LIMITED | Too many requests | Implement exponential backoff and reduce the request rate. |
Report to Zscaler Support with the correlation_id information from the response.
| 500 | INTERNAL_ERROR | Unexpected server error |

audit-logging.statement: All operations log the tenant ID, trace ID, API client ID, client IP address and the change details.

quotes: Audit logging: All operations log tenant ID, trace ID, API client ID, client IP address, and the change details (i.e., what was created, updated, or deleted).

no-client-support.statement: None of the pinned Python SDK, Go SDK, MCP server, ZIA provider or ZPA provider references the Event Monitoring paths, so the API is reached only by direct HTTP calls.
